rules.title: Documentation transition baseline is immutable except by accepted contract change
Document IDs must be unique and valid
Documentation index must cover the current Markdown inventory
V2 front matter required for new or migrated documents
Durable document filenames must not encode manual revisions
Required review dates must be present and current
Scope and applies-to values must be registered
Supersession references must be valid and reciprocal
New technical artifacts are forbidden under PROJECT_DOCS
Registered document types must resolve to an existing template
Document type and status must be registered
Actual scope matches accepted scope
No unrelated side changes
Applicable ADRs, governance and standards are satisfied or updated
Code, contracts, tests, fixtures, evidence and documentation agree
Required profiles were executed and evaluated
No open tool or execution error
All blocking results are resolved
Non-blocking findings are assessed and tracked
Dependencies and structural changes followed their lifecycle
Version, Project-New and managed-project impact is assessed
Debt, risks and deferrals are registered
No secret, forbidden runtime artifact or foreign change is included
No unsupported maturity, security, persistence, strict-gate or delivery claim exists
Engineering evidence is complete
Qualification profile is required for every accepted change
Governance migration, strict promotion and periodic audit require the audit profile
Release changes require audit and release profiles
Release candidates require audit and release profiles
Every path must be covered by a registered directory area
Case-colliding paths are forbidden
Managed-project directory deviations must be valid and unexpired
Technical files require an explicit technical documentation area
Byte-identical duplicates require a declared derivation or allowance
Generated, runtime and temporary paths must not be tracked
Symlinks are forbidden unless a profile explicitly permits them
Backup, copy, editor and temporary artifact names are forbidden
Required root files and directories must exist
Root files and directories must be registered for the profile
Baseline-only transition areas cannot grow silently
File types must be allowed by the registered directory area
Quality Rule Catalog entries must satisfy the registered schema and vocabularies
Gate descriptors must satisfy the registered gate model
Rule IDs and Gate IDs must be valid and unique
Rule-to-gate and gate-to-rule references must be reciprocal and resolvable
Every catalog rule must resolve to an existing normative source section
Accepted material drift requires a complete amendment
Qualification, temporary document disposition and archive closure
Sprint identity and canonical paths
Required sprint documents and metadata
Definition of Done completeness
Definition of Ready completeness
Drift result must use the controlled vocabulary
Crossed target completion requires a current drift review
Sprint documents are discoverable in the documentation index
Measurable milestone contract
Problem and solution space separation
Single current status and valid lifecycle values
Every Java and tooling test artifact is registered exactly once
Suite runner, profile, scope and entrypoint references are valid
Surefire-only baseline is explicit and no Failsafe execution is invented
Suite result states distinguish pass, failure, skip, abort, non-execution and tool error
Every source fixture has one canonical registered path and owner
Expected-case catalogs cover pass, finding and tool-error paths
Golden fixtures have a consumer and reviewed mutation policy
Suite environment requirements and runtime class are explicit
Coverage tool and thresholds remain unresolved until a separate policy is accepted
The current test inventory is sealed without path renames or a big-bang suite migration
Classification, evidence and completion identities are consistent
Every required profile has all registered qualification checks
Qualified completion has no blocking execution or unresolved tool error
Engineering qualification wiring remains read-only and registry-consistent
